chunks: And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a man: is it permissible for him to perform salat (prayer) while there is an open muṣḥaf in front of him in the direction of his qiblah? He said: “No.”
I said: Even if it is in its cover? He said: “Yes.”
And about a man performing salat (prayer) while in front of him there is a basin containing perfume, he said: “Yes.”
I said: He performs salat (prayer) while in front of him there is a brass censer? He said: “Yes.”
He said: I said: Then if there is fire in it? He said: “He should not perform salat (prayer) until he moves it away from his qiblah.”
And about salat (prayer) in a garment whose decorative marking contains the image of a bird or something else, he said: “No.”
And about a man wearing a ring in which there is an engraving of the image of a bird or something else, he said: “Salat (prayer) is not valid with it.”

key_terms.مُصْحَفٌ: a written copy of the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray with an open Qur'an, fire, or images in front of you or on your clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about objects and images in front of a person or on what he wears during salat (prayer). It distinguishes between what is permitted and what invalidates or prevents salat (prayer), such as an open muṣḥaf before the worshipper, fire directly in front of him, and garments or rings bearing animate images.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.780 - Ammar ibn Musa asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about whether it is permissible for a man to pray with an open Qur'an in front of him facing the qibla.
I (Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if it is in its cover?"

Imam (as) said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) then asked about praying with a bowl containing perfume in front of him.

Imam (as) said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if there is a censer made of brass in front of him?"

Imam (as) said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if it has fire in it?"

Imam (as) said: ‘He should not pray until it is moved away from his qibla.’
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked about praying in a garment with the image of a bird or other figures on its design.

Imam (as) said: ‘No’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked about wearing a ring with an engraved image of a bird or other figures while praying.
Imam (as) said: ‘Prayer is not valid with it.’
